posts.title: Why we cut cable while you wait
posts.excerpt: At Kairo Supply, measuring and cutting cable to length at our counter bay saves contractors cash flow, workshop space, and jobsite scrap.
posts.content:
Walk into almost any electrical contractor lockup in Ostwick and you will find partial drums of cable sitting against the wall. Coils of flex, half-used drums of twin and earth, and unfinished reels of armoured cable often sit untouched for months. Every metre of that conductor represents trade capital tied up on a workshop floor, paid for upfront on invoice and rarely matching the run length of the next installation. When Ruth Abernethy established Kairo Supply at Unit 3, Brennan Yard in 2004, eliminating that redundant stock was one of the core principles set for our trade counter.

Standard wholesale practice has long pushed contractors toward purchasing complete drums. While full reels suit bulk commercial containment runs, standard domestic and light commercial jobs rarely require whole drums of heavy or specialist flex. Purchasing excess material forces trade businesses to carry inventory risk and clutter their vans. At Brennan Yard, our system is arranged so contractors purchase only what an installation plan requires. Instead of storing expensive surplus cable in your workshop, you collect the exact metreage needed for the job in hand.

Tomás Rocha manages our cutting bay, operating heavy cutters over a steel bench marked with calibrated measurements. Every cut from our master reels is completed while you wait at the trade counter, taking ten minutes or less. Trade account holders pay a cut fee of €0, with cutting available for any length from 5 metres upward. We stock and cut all standard conductor sizes from 1.0 mm² up to 35 mm², covering lighting circuits, socket rings, sub-mains, and heavy commercial equipment feeds.

The immediate practical advantage for contractors is preserving working cash flow. Rather than tying up credit on full reels of heavy conductors, you allocate funds only to the cable installed and billed that week. In addition, carrying tailored coils keeps trade vehicles organized and prevents excess axle weight. Instead of wrestling heavy wooden drums around a van floor, your team collects clean, taped coils clearly marked with your site reference. When you arrive on site, the coil unrolls cleanly without tangles or awkward offcut waste.

Accurate cutting also addresses jobsite waste. Discarded offcuts represent one of the most persistent losses on building sites. Shorter lengths left on a drum rarely match subsequent projects and often sit until cleared as scrap at a fraction of their original purchase value. By cutting directly to your schedule from master drums, Tomás ensures that copper is used efficiently and contractors leave with precisely what their installation drawings specify.

For contractors managing tight morning schedules, custom lengths can also be ordered in advance through our job pack service. If you submit your cutting list by 15:00, Aoife Brennan and Tomás Rocha cut, coil, and pack your cable beside your required accessories, ready for collection when our doors open at 06:30. Whether you wait ten minutes at the counter or collect from our lockers at 06:00, cable cut to the metre keeps your jobs moving across Ostwick without wasted materials.
